segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: I’m thankful you two came. Before we begin, I’m going tell you two what I said the reason for this. These learners… some time they’re going to start listening to this to discover how the real Cherokee language is. And also, if you two have grandkids, some time they will start to listen. Sometime if they want to hear you two speak, they will also allow them to listen to this.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: That’s important.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: As we begin, as we begin now, tell me you two’s full names in English. Starting with Ray.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Johnny Ray Ross.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Now in Cherokee.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Richard Lee Ross. Siquanid.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Siquanid, yeah. Where were you born?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Tahlequah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: What year was that?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: So, you’re one year older than me. What about you?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Tahlequah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: What year was that?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: You two can help each other out with answering this. What was it like when you two grew up and where did you two grow up?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: I grew up in Greasy. We grew up in Greasy.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: The same.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Yeah the same.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: About that, how did you two grow up?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: As for me, I used to think it was good but I found out later, it was hard. That’s what I remember.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: We didn’t it we had it hard huh?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Not really.. yeah that .. [inaudible]..

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: We didn’t know what we was doing was hard.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: We also didn’t have all the things they have to play with like these days. What.. What could you all do and what did you all do back then?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: As for me, that huh tires, and we rolled them around back then. And also, those hub caps we ran around with those pretending we were cars, ain’t it back then. Just different things and we were playing ball then but it was good back then. I don’t think any different about things today.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: It wasn’t that dangerous back then.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Not really at all.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Did you all put dust in the tires that we’re talking about?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Just like they were running like they were smoking, we had those tires filled with dust.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: How many in all were in your family?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Eight.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: You all are Cherokee speakers?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: All.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: When you all were playing and gathered at you all’s home, do you all speak all Cherokee?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: All Cherokee.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: What was it like back then when you all met?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: What was it like?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Huh d…

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Good.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: It was good?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Good. We played around and talk, there was nothing back.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: I guess you all played a lot of ball, too. Reason being, all of you all were good ball players growing up.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Mhmm.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: What about, can you two tell me a little bit about how you two’s dad lived his life. I knew him but you two ahead and tell me.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: It was really hard, but that’s what he had to do. He would make ties and posts. He had to farm and just different things for our benefit he would find is what he would do.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: That’s the way it was we worked really hard growing up. Just when you could raised them up, a fence post. We had to raise them up and work.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Then you had to work.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Yeah we helped him everywhere.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: He didn’t farm just a little bit, huh. He planted a lot, huh.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Yeah big.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: He planted different things. Corn, cucumbers, different things. Potatoes.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Corn ain’t it?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: And in the winter we dug potatoes. We would put them underneath the house.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Would they make it through winter?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Good.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: They turned out good.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Some talk about and say Dad dug, he would dig and he would put hay in there and that’s where they put those potatoes they would say.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: I don’t remember us putting hay in there.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: All I remember, is that we put in under the house.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: So he really liked to play ball, too, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Very much. That's all he would do. When we used to play ball before the time came he would be saying where are we going to be going.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: That’s what I remember most about him was him playing ball. Sometimes he would make those to hit with.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Bats.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Yeah that.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: How long did it take him when he started?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Not very long, I really don’t remember. But like axe handle, it was quite a long time. He used to teach me, I can do that also, I can make them. I can do that, too, that’s what I was taught. I quickly tried, I still remember what I was taught. Like bows, how to do them, I can make them.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: And about you two’s moms, she looked after the house ain’t it?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Yeah, she was the cook.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: That was good cooking huh?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: I couldn’t figure out how we could feed that many people. When they played ball, it was even more, and it was “All of y’all come and eat.”

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: There at the old ball field, that’s where y’all lived.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Across from there.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: I used to spend the night there and go home with those boys sometimes. There was a spring just below there.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: And on this side it was a place to swim.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: How old were we all, Ray when we had a place where we played ball?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: We were just about 11 years old ain’t it, back then ain’t it and then we moved way over there.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: From what I can remember it was already made.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Yep.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Me too.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: It was until… around the 70s when we moved.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Then Ross Mountain.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Was it then they stopped playing ball?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: When y’all left did someone or buy it what?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: It belongs to two people.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: The late Barney.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Barney and Cecil.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: It was in the middle..

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: That's where it met.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: ..where they threw from (pitcher’s mound)

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: … the fence went.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: They put a fence there.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: It's a wonder they didn’t fighter over since they were white people.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: What about you.. Huh .. where did you got to school?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Greasy.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: When you finished there, where?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Cave Springs.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: What about you?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: The same, at Greasy. UG they called back then.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: What about when you finished high school, what did you do?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: I went to Okmulgee for a little while.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: We went.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Just for a little while.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: So y’all just went there and back.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: This is how it happened, I don’t know if you remember Ray. I don’t know if it was Tommy’s room was were in.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: They sung ‘Take Me Home Country Road’. That’s when we decided to come home.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: When we was going school, we went to intramurals and was the softballs champions, huh.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Uh-huh, yeah. Yeah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: We left here and won it.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Faye was the leader huh, the coach.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Uh-huh. Faye was really funny. And Dallas Proctor.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Uh-huh.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: You could only see one, when he’s with a girl, two hours later he would be with Dallas. We had fun there. When we came back, what did you do?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Well, I just went to work. I worked in Ft. Smith quite awhile then in 71’.. Thereabouts in 71’ I joined the armed services.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Later.. It had to be later because we graduated in 71’.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Yeah it was 72’. Yeah in 72’ I joined the armed services and the reason was there was nothing else to do there. And I was doing wrong things, getting into trouble that’s why. Another reason my brother was in the service. One day I came home, I said “Mom, I’m going to go look for my brother.” She said “huh?” Yes, I’m going to look for my brother. I joined at that time. Real quick they sent me to Kentucky way. Ft. Polk, then when I came home to over seas, where I got overseas company, I think a company my brother was there.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: There, too, he was your brother?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Uh-huh same company, uh there just different unit, about six month’s he got moved my bed next door where they little place with rooms there he moved in.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: You found him?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Uh-huh, yeah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: How long did you stay in?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Me, three years I stayed in, he, too, I think stayed that long.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: He was like that, he would leave at times.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Yeah, yeah.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: All the time.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: That’s the way he was, for himself he thinks.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: That’s where we were talking about Okmulgee when we quit, we came back, but Faye he went some place else.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Uh yeah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: How about you, when you got done, what did you do?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Same, I just went to work. For a little while. Later I went to school, same place you all went to school at Okmulgee schooling. After I left there, I went to a different place for school. I've got a lot of schooling. After a time I left home, too. I done good. For I went to school to be a auto repair mechanic. Then I opened my own place in Ft. Gates, Texas. After I left there in the year of ‘85, I came home. Then went to carpenter work, building houses. I done good. Then I started my own company. ‘Ross Mountain Construction’.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Uh, did you like it when you were overseas Ray?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Uh… not really.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Where were you really at?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: First I left, left Oakland now to Vietnam there a little while got defer to Korea, there for over 13 months was there.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Did you see any fighting, while you were in Vietnam?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: No. That’s when troops were starting to come home, the end.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Oh..

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: That’s why, I went to Korea.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: What did you think about Korea?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Same really. For Vietnam when you first get there it’s weird, for the smell just everything even people, Korea was similar to that but little cleaner.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Was it their homes in Vietnam?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Uh-huh.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Not good, their homes?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Reckon good homes for themselves. But built with mud like.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Uh.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Built homes.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Did they accept you good?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Some did, some. But you couldn’t accept any person, you didn’t know.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: You didn’t know if he was enemy so it was dangerous?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Yeah. It was dangerous, and-and Korea there, too, “the line” us where I was “--------” standing there all alone with my rifle. I could hear north side talking or hollering. They were in tanks would stop and turn them around. And they’d have radios on with speakers, at times they would call somebody’s name, and where your home was everything.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: They knew all that much?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Uh-- and they had holes in the ground with tunnels”-------” at times they’ll walk by there but you don’t know who they are, can’t tell difference between north and south Korean.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: You were South Korea side?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Uh-huh there’s spies.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Ohh – you all were in dangerous spot.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: It was dangerous, but still better than--

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Than Vietnam.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Uh-huh.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Did you sleep good though?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Yeah. At times, about one or two o’clock we’d hear loud boom, we’d get up, be running all over. Yeah good.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Ohh---. When we were talking about gardening, did your mom put stuff up?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: They would can stuff at the time.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: They would can different stuff, even wild stuff. Like huckleberry and…
Blackberry and--.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Was there huckleberry behind…

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: No it wasn’t.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: There towards’s Cave Springs we hunted for huckleberry.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Ah--- I never went there. Sander's flat is where was got ours.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Going up hill.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: I'm going to ask you, where you all lived in that hollow tree there were snakes. Rattlesnakes there. Uh have you ever been there and them?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: I have.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: All the time, we were around that area. We used to play in that area.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: You weren’t thinking about that?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: The holes between big boulder, we played inside.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s where they lived snakes.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: But you didn’t think about stuff like that. I guess that’s why they didn’t bother you.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Really, though did you all see them?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Were they big?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Some were. Sometime Darrel Hardbarger the late. He would go there and kill them for the skin, sometime pretty big.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Yeah, they were big. The biggest one, about two years ago, I caught one this big? Took me two tries to get it in the back of my pickup truck it was that big.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: You were crazy.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Me too, we were cutting fence post at Starr Killer, there was a little puddle of water with weeds and green grass. There in that puddle of water, we were playing in. We found one rattlesnake we were playing with then another one we were playing with.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: [laughing] Both of you were crazy. They’re my kinfolks, that’s why I'm calling them that.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: There at the lumber yard in Stilwell is where I took that snake.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: That big one we’re talking about?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: That big one, they were this [gestures] big, what would you call them on diamondback the diamonds were this [gestures] big.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Gah-lee. You didn’t skin it?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: No I was going to work remodeling, I didn’t have time.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: How many did he have---?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: He didn’t have any, they were broke off.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Uhh---, wonder why?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Maybe he’d been run over or something.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Uh-huh.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: I looked at it, I clubbed it and it was on, it’s back in the truck, its head was this big.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Gah-lee.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Lot of people seen it, in that yard owner we went and looked at it, they all gathered around like hogs feeding as they looked at it. I never paid attention to it, what the that rattlesnake had all different colors green and blue all different colors, green and blue all different diamonds and around it sure was beautiful.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Huh--- I never thought about that?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Hadn’t?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: To me, it just looked black.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: It does look like it.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Uh---

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: But if you pay attention to it. It has about five different colors on the edge of it.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Huh--

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Green, purple, orange, brown, and black.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Huh. How about, some eat that meat, have you ever tried it?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: I have, it’s really good taste.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: It’s good?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Yeah, something like when they make stew, stew meat it tastes like, some like it. Then when you take second bite it’s a little different but still good as for taste.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: How do you cook it?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: That I don’t know. I visited someone and they had it and I ate with him, and that’s how it was. Some what like bbq, it was, but it was good. Or maybe I might have been starving.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: How about when your father was gardening how was he breaking the ground, a horse?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Horse we used for plowing. And plow.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: When we moved up higher, it was same with horse.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: His garden was bigger when you moved there wasn’t it?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Oh yeah. It was ¼ acre.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Uh-huh.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: It was.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Did you ever give it a try at it?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: I have.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: And you Ray?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Hu-uh.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Faye did though give it a try didn’t he?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Yeah. It was good, you’d think we were standing, breaking plow.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: How about did you all have a wagon back then ?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Uh --- what kind of wagon?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Pulled by a horse.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Pulled by a horse? Never, did we have one of those?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: You all didn’t have your foot out that far?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: No, not that far out.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Did you have something to ride in?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Later on, after we moved there, I was the first to get one.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: What kind was it?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: ‘61 Chevy, two door bubble top.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Easy, did you learn to drive it?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Where we were working the let use a big truck, picking-up rocks out in the field that’s when I learned to drive. I got my first car.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: What was it like, when you said bubble-top?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: It wasn’t like you’re thinking. [laughter] It didn’t have no bubble. [laughter] Like that hard top its that back window it’s like this [gestures], bubble-top would wrap around some. It’s not really a bubble-top.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: That’s what I thought it was.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Yeah, I seen that in your eyes. [laughter]

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: I could see it floating. I could just see you trying to drive it.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Like a floater.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: How much did you pay for it, back then, do you remember?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: $250 I’m thinking my late father went and bought it. That ᎦᎸᏥ is his name, is that mink?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Uh-huh.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: That’s who he bought it from. That's when I was in ninth grade at Cave Springs then when he gave it to me.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Uh---, everywhere, did you run then?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Beaver Gap. [laugh]

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: You didn’t know how then Ray.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Probably not.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: I taught them how.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Standard, they were all back then?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Yeah almost all, but my car was automatic.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Oh---, it was automatic.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: All the time, I was watching for it to shift like you would shift yourself, that’s what it’s going to do, that shifter I thought. But it wasn’t like that.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: How much did you pay for gas back then?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Uh---not even---see---.87 cents I think or .89 cents either one at Barney Girdner’s where it was.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Myself, what I remember .18 cents, I remember.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Myself, .24 cents, I remember.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: When it went up then to .29 cents, .30, and .32 cents.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: I talk about this all the time with one quarter, you could buy a drink, chips, and honey bun.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Yeah, yeah.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: That’s what we would do when we picked strawberries. When I took in if I had a quarter it bothered me.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Where did you pick strawberries?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Up above us, he had a patch, the late Barney.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: He had a big patch.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: It looked good, I thought.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: We just walked up the hill.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Up the hill, we go.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: That, already on the hill, you lived wgeb Pete Ford had his patch? Road edge of.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Huh-uh, back there we lived, they picked us up in and took us there.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: I have, too, picked when Pete Ford had patch. That's where I starved gonna feed me, Mom I thought I was in line. When time to order, what are you doing, she said. Ordering I said, nothing money you got, a little. Go pick she told me.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s what they tell you. I sometimes would be playing, my dad would find. Then here next to him you pick he told me.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Yeah --- [laughing] where he’d watch you if you were picking, working he’d set you next to him.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: I know, hogs, he had your late dad, uh winter towards he’d kill them, didn’t he?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Uh-huh.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Did y’all help?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Yeah, scraping, everything, everybody helped then, that I remember.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: And women what we cut up they would carry away put it up or they would cook it, everybody helped.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Still, the one they called smoke he have it outside?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Uh---

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: That’s where he kept the meat?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Uh-huh.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Smokehouse.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Did they smoke it, smokehouse they call it?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Huh-uh, where it was kept.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Salt, they would put or rub on it.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Uh, salt lot of we would put on like it was caked on then meat then salt on top.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Winter, it would make through in there?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Uh-huh.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: How about the uh intestines?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: That, too.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: That they would grab before anybody, Mom did.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Yeah, forced and warm, they’d do. It's easy to fix them, they would get a little stick, stick it all the way through, turn the stick certain way pull the inside out and wash them all.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Did you like to eat them?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: I did.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: I did, too. While they were cooking, I didn’t like.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: What about, this big something they stuffed inside, do you remember?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Uh---

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Like say cornmeal, something mixed with cornmeal, bigger intestines they would stuff inside.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Sausage like?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Uh-huh.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Also, blood they would use.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Oh, is that right?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Blood, they would put inside.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Then tie the ends.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: That’s like what we call weenies, that’s what it was.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Have you ate them?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: I have, I liked them. But we had too we were starving, I don’t know if I could one today.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Did they put blood in it?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Yeah, when it sets, it would set in little while.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Did they cook it, or what?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Uh-huh.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: That what I liked, them intestines.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Uhh.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: They’re all different kinds, the stomach is different from intestines. There's difference one is large stomach and one is smaller. The smaller ones were goooood.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Did you eat them?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Yeah. We didn’t throw anything away except bones and hair.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: How about they call hoghead cheese?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Head baked, is what it’s called.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Is that what they call it? Head baked.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Uh-huh.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: When I was a boy, I really, liked that, I don’t know if I could eat it now a days.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Me too.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: I really want some, wonder where we can find some?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: They don’t make it anymore, do they?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: No, only some stores have hoghead. But it’s not that good, I've tried it.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: It’s not good?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Different in taste, I guess. Long time ago it might have been the same. Still starving.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: It wasn’t really starving.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: They fed us then.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: We ate three times a day.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Go catch a chicken and cut it’s head off, they would say.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Today these kids won’t eat like that.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: I don’t like that, they’ll say.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: They don’t like hardly anything.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Then you to go get what they want.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: They’re really spoiled, when we were growing up, what ever our mother’s cooked is what we ate.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Or you didn’t eat.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Right. I think a lot about that, when we were growing up. I didn’t eat that, uhh I forgot what they call it, but what would you call corn dodgers?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Corn bread, boiled.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Oh, corn bread boiled isn’t it? I just had some of them, when we had our singing. I don’t know who made them but it had beans in them.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Were they round or what?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Same as you fix biscuits, only corn bread after that boiling water put them in so they don’t spoil, that’s how they cook.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: How about what they call dog head?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: That’s what it is. But they call them different names.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: And they call them bean ball, too. Myself I like bean ball, really like them. I'll stick it with a fork, put salt on it, and eat it that way.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: That’s what we ate as we were growing up.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Yeah, I remember all the time Ruby your mom, cucumber, and green tomatoes she ask for.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Cucumber, they would call her.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: We would stay with different families, but all were family.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Uh-huh.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Your mom, and my dad were family.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Little while ago the I talking to we’re kin, too, I find out, a Chuculate, Watie’s sister.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Oh-oh, that one from Marble City way.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Uh, your dad sometimes he would coach ball team didn’t he?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Uh-huh.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: He himself used to play, did he play first or where?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: He would pitch.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: He was a pitcher and John my uncle, John Jr’s dad he played first base. I didn’t recognize he was standing by close. Last time I seen him he was big John Sr. He looks like he might be sickly, looking at him.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: He did get sick.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Really?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: But right now, he don’t look like he’s sick.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: We were in the same grade, going to school.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Really, same time? Isn’t our youngest we call Nellie are you about the same age?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Yeah some age.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: That’s what I thought.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Ragson?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Uhh, last weekend, he was here.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Really?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Yeah, he came in.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: That’s back in ‘85 I was talking about where I was, I came to Port Arthur, Texas. I couldn’t find a place to spend the night. Last time I talked with him, if you’d said, if you knew, just over there, where Holiday Motel is, I live right behind it, he told me.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: We went there where we lived.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: I went around that way I came to Port Arthur.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Doctors, did they take you as you grew up?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: No, just the medicine they knew about. As for myself, really I went through hard times, sickly bad I was, I guess it meant for me to be healthy. I think I was almost two years old before I got out the hospital after been born. A little while, I had left my body they told me, they had given up on me. When, I think they unhooked me. That's when I heard the prettiest sound what my mother told me, you gave the best cry you ever had when they unhooked you.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Do you remember any of the medicine they used as you were growing?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: I was taught a lot.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: You still remember some?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Still, I still use. That's why I'm still sitting here, I was telling you when they gave up on me. They told me after so many months, I won’t be able to stand or get up from bed. That's all I used, it’s been three years when they told me, but I'm still walking.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: What do you use, if you can talk about it?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: It’s a few different things, but I can’t talk about it. Unless I treat someone and fix it for. But it’s different things, “ᎦᏃᏍᏓᏆᎳ” they call, I don’t what to call it, it grows by creek or water. Sort of like knotty bark tree, they’re round, that’s one I use, it gives you strength, like your bones get weak it’s for that. It's hard growing tree.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Is that a hackberry?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Hackberry, yeah-yeah. It's kind of like slick bark with little knots. Use bark-boiled. Take bark from east side of tree, with prayer to God, when you make medicine some don’t do that today.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: All they do is get it?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: They’re just after money.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: How about the ones diabetics?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: That, too.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Still the same?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: ᎧᏩᏯ or huckleberry.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: “ᎪᎳ ᎬᎾᏍᎩ” “ᎧᏩᏯ”, different things, but best is “ᎪᎳ ᎬᎾᏍᎩ” - ᎧᏩᏯ roots boiled. Some are roots, some bark, different ways to fix.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Do you boil the huckleberry roots?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Uh-huh.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Do you take it as you get thirsty for water?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Take it like as you would drink water. You take it three times a day, but they’ll usually tell you how to use it.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Can’t I just go get it myself the huckleberry root?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Yeah, you can go get it, but that’s all it be just getting it. Prayer goes with it all in Cherokee. That I know, the way I was taught asking good for him to accept the medicine to make the person to get well, is what you ask first, before working the medicine. There'e a lot that goes out and get medicine, just like you said, can’t I just go get it myself. If you know it, and someone ask’s you to go get it then you can go get it, but you can’t make it medicine.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: So if I went out and got it myself, it won’t help me?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Huh-uh.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: It has to be someone that work’s it?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Someone that work’s it, has to make it for you, you have to ask if he would make it for you. It has to be yourself not someone else. Same as it says in the Bible, you have to do it yourself, nobody can do it for you. That's the way it is with medicine, you have to ask someone if he would do it for you.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: How about you, did you pick up any on about medicine work?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Huh-uh, I've heard them talking about it, but I wasn’t really listening.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Lots of us have done that, now we’ve lost it.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: What did you say they call hackberry?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Uh-huh what I was telling you Michael, ᎦᏌᏗ that, too, is medicine.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Is that elderberry?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Uh, it’s like “ᎧᎾᏏᏓ”. At first flowering. It flowers just before same kind white flower, dogwood “ᎧᎾᏏᏓ”. It flowers just before, white flowering you can see long ways, that’s “ᎪᏌᏗ” that, too, is medicine for diabetes.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Is that not elderberry?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Maybe, they used to make jelly and jam with it, you can use it for.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: George used that stuff. Where I used to get that, this time it didn’t do any good, I didn’t find any.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: A lot, that happens at times, I’ve noticed. Same with mushrooms, wisi, where they used to come up. Where we’d get, they didn’t hardly make any. I don’t know what happened, but it knows.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: What you’re talking about, do you all like?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Uh-huh. As long as it’s “ ᎤᏂᏜᏫ” or “ᏫᏏ”. That’s all I know, that’s probably what got me through starvation.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: “ᎤᏂᏍᏉᎵ” what about? They call morel mushroom.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Morel, uh.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Do you still find them?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Myself, I only found two of them, about this tall and this big. And that like deer antlers. It is good to eat, too.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: It has a lot on it. That's what Ann said, it’s good to eat, but I’ve never ate any. But the late Roger’s daughter, we called Justie, she was talking about, says she likes it.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Deer antlers is they call in English. I forget a lot of things.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: I didn’t know you could eat that stuff.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: You didn’t?

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Is it really mushroom, what you’re telling?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Yeah. They grow like deer antlers.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Gollee.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Just like the “ᎤᏂᏍᏉᎵ” or morel mushroom.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: You used to find enough of them to eat.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Do you still go out in the woods, Ray?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: I don’t remember the last time, I been in the woods.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Myself, where I was born, is where I bounced around.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: So you’re not able to grow a garden?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Huh-uh. But I still walk in the woods. Where I got my horses penned. Right by is where I hunted mushrooms with my sister, Lilly. Or when I hunt medicine close by.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Are you two by yourselves now?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Uh-huh.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: You’ve traveled a lot haven’t you Ray?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: What do they call in Cherokee, California?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: You’ve lived there.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: How long?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Eight years.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Did you like it?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Yeah, it was good, I liked it, but it was expensive.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: So it was expensive?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Yeah, it was.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Were you working there?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Huh-uh, I wasn’t working. But my wife was working.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: What did you like about it there?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: I liked the weather, and if had to go out it was close, sight seeing, ocean, baseball like Padres and Angels.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: How about football?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Yeah, football, too.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Did you go watch the games?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Yeah, Chargers. When they were there. I did watch basketball games, too, Los Angeles. I like that kind of stuff.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: How about Disney World, did you go there?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Yeah, two or three times.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Myself, this past summer, I had planned on taking them out there. But I was looking on newsbreak, they were closing things so I didn’t take them.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Or you were just tight with your money.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Yeah. But I think they opened things back up.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: We went to Tennessee and North Carolina. How about you, have traveled much and seen a lot where did you live mostly after you left?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: I guess Texas, but there’s only three states I haven’t been, I haven’t been to Rhode Island, Connecticut, and Delaware, I haven’t been. But the rest I've been.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Did you work these places?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: I worked, some traveling, but mostly working.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Where did you stay the longest?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Over in Texas.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: What did you like about it?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: I guess all I had. All I had was $60.00 that I worked hard for, when I left. Then I got on the bus, cost me $400, so I just had $20.00 left when I got off. You sure messed up I was telling myself. Going on in about two months, I had a garage.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: So you really found a good thing?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: How about things you could do, what did you like?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Just construction work.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Did you go watch football games sometimes?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: No I didn’t. All I was doing then was repair vehicles, cause that what I went to school for. I guess what they done for me, to have a good like is what I really liked.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: How about what we call hobby, do you have?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Myself, my hobby is horses, like breaking them is what I like the most.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: How many do you own?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Now just two. I sold some when I took ill. I couldn’t take care of them. Now I want them horses back now that I’m doing better.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: How about you Ray, you got any?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: No horses.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Do you just sit around watch TV or what?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Yeah, at times I watch TV, or clean house.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Me too, I really like to clean house.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: When I had my own place, I worked in the yard all the time, didn’t run out of work.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: So you couldn’t just sit around doing nothing?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Yeah, if I sit doing nothing I would be dozing.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: I have horses, too, seven but I'm going to sell them.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Really?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Riding horses, or is it them that was in the pasture with the long ears spotted, donkeys and mules?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: No, there’s only one mule. The rest are real horses, part mustangs, but they’re all getting tired of them.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: What kind of mustangs, Nebraska or Utah’s?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Utah’s two mares paint I have, I said I was going to sell them, now, they want them.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: What used to be hog pen, is that where dirt thrower used to live in the area? Back side where that pond is used to be hogs.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: All woods used to be.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Really?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: That Linda’s husband, Linda Wilson, he operates bulldozer he’s ub Alaska, I’m waiting on him I'm going to lease bulldozer have him clear it all. Then I'm going to buy cows in spring. So I have to sell my horses, they’re really pretty horses but never rode or anything.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: I've only seen some, yeah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: What us Cherokee believe in like spooks or ghost’s, have you seen that?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: I've seen a lot.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Talk to us about it.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: One time this person I was walking home on the road. We had been coon hunting with my late grandpa’s place. I was walking to home, walking by this house, I looked in that way thought they were all sleeping they were elders. I looked that way and seen a little light in one room. I took a good look, there was an old lady sitting in the middle of the bed, like on her knees, what is she doing I thought I was watching her in her hand was kerosene lamp moving it back and forth and I was getting the chill’s but I wanted to know what she was doing. After a while she was doing this with the lamp raising it up, as I was watching her she changed she had longer hair and it was flowing like it was windy. Something like if one was underwater how it flows, that’s what it was doing sitting on the bed as I was watching her. Little while she moved her head that’s when I thought she’d seen me, she looked right at me. She done this, that’s when everything went dark, but I could still see her hair that’s the last time I looked, I took off running to the house, I thought she had seen me. She was fixing to change to something else.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: She was getting ready to change.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Yeah, she ready to change, to go some place. As for me I was running home.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: That’s where you headed, too?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Yeah that’s where I headed, too, I was sure she’d seen me. There's more but this is one I remember the best, she was ready to take off flying, her hair was flowing her body was moving with the lamp she was holding in her hand.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: I've forgot things like that, I’m getting forgetful. But I do remember this, when we were little my brother and me, we were in our room in the old house by the ball field, the rest were in the living room and kitchen. We were playing by the old TV, I was showing him the magazine, he was sitting by the window, then my sister Ollie was gone. Something was looking in the window up close I seen, I just dropped the magazines look what looking in the I said to him, we both took off running to the living room. The adult’s went in there looked around, but find nothing, but it was looking through the window.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: That person had already changed to something else.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: That’s what you would say, isn’t it?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Uh-huh, that’s what I was saying that one was getting ready to change to something else. The call shift shaper or is it shape shifter, that’s changing. We got changeling the “ᎠᏂᎦᎳᎾ”

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: What is that really?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: They’re the ones that changes into fire, hasn’t been that long ago, I kinda thought I knew who it was, these two that were left, were what they were. They had one of them, they had his body and I was there from the east a light was coming, we saw several of us. Right where the body was at his home the light stopped above the body. That was the sister to this other person, this man he came to see her body, the light came, stopped above the body at the rafters.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: The woman was one, too?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Uss, the two both were. The last I know.

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: The other came to get something didn’t he?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Uhh.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: That’s what they say, I’ve heard for his benefit or help.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Uhh, for his help, as they go and bother people that’s for their help, for they will get bad ill. As a person is sickly, that’s where they come to feed, get their help to stay well, till that sick person dies.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: I’m going to tell you something. This still happens to me, when I go to sleep at night and wake in the morning, it’s like someone pinched my toes. And one time my back was like someone put a bruise on it, is it like that?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Someone is bothering you, is what they say. Sometimes it can be someone close to you.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: That’s still happening to me at the present, I’m just depending on God’s help. I don’t condemn people that’s doing that to get their help, that’s their decision.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: That’s what they were given.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: As for myself I’m depending on my God.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Just depend on him or to move it away?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Just to get through it.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: For him to help you? You think about it, ask him to move it away for you. Instead of his help, ask him to move it away.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: That’s where I’m coming up short. Again one more story of what you have witnessed.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: One time that strawberry we were picking we were saying that up hill road by the house I was walking, nighttime I walked all the time. That’s where I was walking that straight away slight curve, little ways goes uphill. Walking there got like itchy feet and chills over body it fot that way. Right going uphill at the start of it, something white I seen, at first paper like I thought. I kept a going after a little bit it was little bigger looked like, but I kept going after a bit a dog, a little one yead big, what it was. Still I kept walking, he was coming towards me, the way I was walking he was coming. What am I going to do I was thinking, he was getting close, he was kind of a big dog, then I didn’t know what to do I couldn’t turn back don’t run is what I was always told, something you going do to yourself if you run. Still he was coming, real loud I whopped that I remember, when I whopped I kicked out. I looked on the edge that dry creekbed he rolled down to it, nothing that I noticed not even kicking him he landed I walked by went uphill when I topped it, I turned around I seen him trying to get up. The more I was bowing going down hill then, after a little I turned my head, he was coming up hill. God dog I was about to run, pretty fast runner I was when I played ball, boy I’m gonna run I kept thinking, but don’t I was always told so I kept walking, and the closer he getting, where it gets sandy where it gets wider close to it I was. I was hearing him breathe like huffing running like. I was scared to turn my head. When I got passed that turnoff to wood cutting used to be. Real close behind he was making that sound now I’m gonna take off running I thought straight to the house I was thinking, but still I didn’t run. Real close he was something I heard in front of me that’s when I stopped they’re going to run into me I thought. It was snarling like a cat but bigger sounded like in front behind dog like there I stood which one’s gonna run into me I thought. One growled close ran by that cat when I turned around now that something white coming behind quickly turned ran after it, to wood we cut going downhill there they went I. There I just stood, I thought boy I shoulda had ran, I’m still waiting I was thinking. Then after a little while after they ran down the hill “Wooooo!” It hollered. Boy that’s when I took off running to the house, there John’s turn off I was past it walking quick, the it was snarling come running behind me that cat after it had ran off that thing, again there I stood firmly. It’s going to jump on me I was thinking. It was snarling ran by where I was standing just little ways it stopped I couldn’t see but snarling it was, little bit as I stood there quiet it got, I started walking close by some footsteps I heard, behind me it was snarling again, then in front of me, that it was doing as I walked “ᏛᏃᏪᎳᏂ ᏣᎵ” his house there by it was a turnoff there it hollered cat I guess you would say, as it snarled there a little trail went that cat. That's what, my uncle “ᏛᏃᏪᎳᏂ” cat helped me I was thinking. There's a lot of things I've witnessed. Boy a lot of things I can talk about. Already that uh Jeffrey, Carl Limore that late picked me up used to, all over we ran, that already got it fixed, this you talk about, one page can you write it he’d say to me. I got a friend in Wichita, Kansas book he write for you if I fix it up he said to me. One page I said, yeah one page not even on back side he said. Boy you don’t want to know too much about me do you Jeff I said to him. What do you mean he said, one page wouldn’t be introduction to who I am I said. Yeah, book made for me he wanted. All night I can sit telling stories.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: I guess we’ll have to cut it off then, now something I'm going to ask you this Cherokee we’re speaking and talking, what’s going to happen do you think?

segments.speaker: johnny-ross
segments.translation: It’s going to run out I think, already it’s going that way where I grew up, we speak there’s two more besides us that’s all that speaks it, the rest English.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Real hard, I guess we’re trying right now Cherokee to speak. They can learn to speak but it will be different how they say it. But happy someone really trying to learn something. Keep it how we speak it or spoke it.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Two, we lost Cherokee speakers this year. That's someone dies we’re losing our language. This one thing I forgot to ask you, did they ever mention it your parents, Cherokee removal if they were in it?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Not as for myself, but that uhh, our grandma’s and grandpa’s have talked about that. That's where uhh, what the name, I forget uhh, Cherry Tree that ball field, that’s about where they say where they came from Cherokee old, they left right about there I was told that.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: What you mentioned, don’t run you were told, that’s what you were taught?

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: That your father.

segments.speaker: richard-ross
segments.translation: Uh-huh, a lot, this wonder things already you might have heard or you have shape shifted.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: I thank you for coming in, we had a good talk.
